items.question: Under COLREG Rule 19, what specific action is required of a vessel which detects by radar alone the presence of another vessel on a collision course forward of the beam, other than a vessel being overtaken?
options: A maneuver to bring the other vessel onto a steady bearing.
A reduction of speed to steerage way only.
Avoid an alteration of course to port.
Maintain course and speed until the other vessel is sighted visually.
items.explanation: Rule 19(d)(i) states that an alteration of course to port shall be avoided for a vessel forward of the beam, other than for a vessel being overtaken.

items.question: What is the primary purpose of the 'Stripping' phase in oil tanker cargo discharge operations?
options: To remove the final remnants of cargo from the tanks that the main pumps cannot reach.
To increase the pressure in the discharge manifold for faster delivery.
To ventilate the tanks to ensure they are gas-free for entry.
To circulate the cargo through the heaters to reduce viscosity.
items.explanation: Stripping involves using smaller capacity pumps or educators to remove the residue that the high-capacity main cargo pumps lose suction on.

items.question: A DSC distress alert has been received on VHF Channel 70. According to GMDSS procedures, what is the first action the OOW should take if the coastal station does not immediately acknowledge?
options: Immediately transmit a DSC Distress Relay to all ships.
Wait a short period and monitor the radiotelephony distress frequency for voice traffic.
Acknowledge the DSC alert immediately via DSC Channel 70.
Reset the VHF unit to clear the alarm and continue the watch.
items.explanation: Ship stations should not acknowledge by DSC but should listen on the associated radiotelephony frequency (VHF Ch 16) for a Distress Acknowledge from a Coast Station.

items.question: In Dynamic Positioning (DP), what is the function of the 'Reference Systems'?
options: To provide the DP controller with the vessel's position and heading.
To calculate the total fuel consumption of the thrusters.
To override the manual joystick in case of emergency.
To manage the power distribution between the switchboards.
items.explanation: Position reference systems (like DGPS, Laser, or Taut Wire) provide the data required for the DP system to calculate position deviations.

items.question: You are the OOW and notice a discrepancy between the GPS position and a visual bearing fix in a narrow channel. What is the most appropriate immediate action?
options: Switch to the secondary GPS and ignore the visual fix.
Reduce speed and use all available means to verify the ship's position.
Call the technician to recalibrate the GPS antenna.
Continue on the GPS track as it is more precise than manual plotting.
items.explanation: Safety of navigation requires cross-checking all available means; a discrepancy necessitates a cautious approach and verification (Bridge Team Management).

items.question: What is the maximum period allowed between fire drills on a cargo ship?
options: One month.
One week.
Three months.
Every time the vessel enters a new port.
items.explanation: SOLAS requires every crew member to participate in at least one fire drill and one abandon ship drill every month.

items.question: A DP vessel experiences a 'Drive-off'. What is the defining characteristic of this failure?
options: The vessel moves away from the target position due to a malfunction in the control system applying excess thrust.
The vessel drifts away from the target position due to a total loss of power.
The vessel's sensors lose signal due to atmospheric interference.
The vessel is pushed off station by extreme weather exceeding thruster capacity.
items.explanation: A drive-off is an active failure where the DP system incorrectly applies thrust, forcing the vessel away from the setpoint.

items.question: While on watch in the North Atlantic, you observe a vessel on your starboard bow showing two all-round red lights in a vertical line. What is your primary obligation under COLREGs?
options: Maintain course and speed as the stand-on vessel.
Sound one short blast and alter course to starboard to pass astern.
Keep out of the way of the other vessel as she is Not Under Command.
Contact the vessel on VHF to request they move out of the channel.
items.explanation: A vessel displaying two all-round red lights in a vertical line is Not Under Command (NUC). Rule 18(a)(i) states a power-driven vessel underway shall keep out of the way of a vessel not under command.

items.question: During a routine inspection of a Lifeboat, you notice the Hydrostatic Release Unit (HRU) for the liferaft has an expiry date that passed last month. What is the correct action?
options: Mark the date in the maintenance log and wait for the annual survey.
Replace the HRU immediately with a new unit or a serviced exchange unit.
Apply a coat of grease to protect it until the next port.
Extend the life of the HRU by signing a waiver in the Deck Logbook.
items.explanation: SOLAS Chapter III requires LSA to be maintained in good working order. HRUs must be replaced or serviced at intervals not exceeding 12 months (or as specified by the manufacturer for disposable units).

items.question: When securing a vessel at a pier, what is the 'Snap-back Zone'?
options: The area where the gangway touches the quay.
The area at the bow where the anchor is dropped.
The potential path of a mooring line if it parts under tension.
The designated smoking area on the main deck.
items.explanation: The snap-back zone is the area where a mooring line is likely to strike with great force if it breaks. Modern guidance suggests the whole mooring deck should be treated as a danger zone.

items.question: Under STCW, what is the minimum required hours of rest for a watchkeeper in any 24-hour period?
options: 8 hours
10 hours
12 hours
14 hours
items.explanation: STCW Code Section A-VIII/1 states that the minimum amount of rest shall be not less than 10 hours in any 24-hour period.

items.question: Which document must be completed when transferring oily bilge water to a shore reception facility?
options: The Cargo Record Book
The Deck Log Book
The Oil Record Book Part I
The Garbage Record Book
items.explanation: MARPOL Annex I requires every oil tanker of 150 GT and above and every ship of 400 GT and above to maintain an Oil Record Book Part I (Machinery Space Operations).

items.question: During a Fire Drill, the OOW finds that a fire extinguisher's pressure gauge is in the 'red' zone. What is the correct immediate response?
options: Shake the extinguisher to stir the powder and re-check.
Report the defect to the Safety Officer and replace the unit with a spare.
Ignore it until the annual shore-based inspection.
Attempt to discharge it to see if it still works.
items.explanation: LSA and FFA must be maintained in a state of readiness. A pressure gauge in the red indicates the unit may not function; it must be reported and replaced per the ship's SMS.

items.question: In a Dynamic Positioning (DP) system, what is the primary purpose of the 'Weighting' or 'Voting' logic when using multiple Position Reference Systems (PRS)?
options: To discard or de-weight a PRS that shows a significant deviation from the others.
To increase the speed of the vessel's movement between waypoints.
To reduce power consumption of the thrusters.
To manually select which GPS antenna is currently active.
items.explanation: DP control systems use median checks and weighting to ensure that a failing or drifting reference system does not compromise the vessel's position.

items.question: Which GMDSS frequency is designated for the distress, urgency, and safety traffic via DSC on VHF?
options: Channel 70
Channel 16
Channel 06
Channel 13
items.explanation: VHF Channel 70 (156.525 MHz) is the dedicated frequency for Digital Selective Calling (DSC).

items.question: When loading a bulk cargo, the 'Trimming' process is primarily performed to:
options: Reduce the risk of cargo shifting by leveling the cargo surface.
Increase the vessel's speed by changing the draft.
Ensure the cargo does not touch the hatch covers.
Prevent the cargo from becoming wet during the voyage.
items.explanation: Trimming levels the cargo to minimize the air void and the potential for a shift that could affect stability.

items.question: According to COLREG Rule 19, a vessel detecting by radar alone the presence of another vessel shall determine if a close-quarters situation is developing. If so, and an alteration of course is necessary for a vessel forward of the beam, what should be avoided?
options: An alteration of course to port.
An alteration of course to starboard.
Decreasing speed.
Stopping the engines.
items.explanation: Rule 19(d)(i) states that an alteration of course to port for a vessel forward of the beam should be avoided, other than for a vessel being overtaken.

items.question: During a routine inspection of an inflatable lifejacket, you find the CO2 cylinder is hand-tight but the green indicator clip is missing. What is the correct immediate action?
options: Remove from service, check cylinder weight, and replace the indicator clip and firing bobbin if necessary
Tighten the cylinder further and return it to the rack
Order a new lifejacket as the warranty is void once the clip is missing
Mark the lifejacket as 'Exercise Use Only' but keep it in the locker
items.explanation: A missing indicator clip suggests the unit may have been partially activated or tampered with. The cylinder must be weighed to ensure it is full, and the firing mechanism must be inspected/reset.

items.question: In the GMDSS system, which frequency is designated for distress, urgency, and safety traffic using Digital Selective Calling (DSC) on the VHF band?
options: Channel 70
Channel 16
Channel 06
Channel 13
items.explanation: Channel 70 (156.525 MHz) is the dedicated frequency for DSC alerts. Voice communication follows on Channel 16.
items.regulation: ITU Radio Regulations / STCW Table A-IV/2

items.question: In Dynamic Positioning (DP), what is the function of the 'Kalman Filter'?
options: To estimate the ship's position and heading by filtering out high-frequency noise caused by waves
To clean the hydraulic oil in the thruster units
To switch between different Differential GPS providers
To calculate the fuel consumption per thruster
items.explanation: The Kalman filter is a mathematical model used to estimate the vessel's state and filter out first-order wave motions so the DP system reacts only to sustained forces.

items.question: During a mooring operation, what is the 'snap-back zone'?
options: The area where a line is likely to recoil with high energy if it parts under tension
The area directly under the winch drum
The space between the fairlead and the bollard
The zone where the tug boat connects the line
items.explanation: If a mooring line parts, it releases stored energy, recoiling (snapping back) toward its anchor points, posing a lethal risk to personnel in that area.

items.question: In a DP system, what does the term 'Redundancy' specifically refer to?
options: The ability of the system to maintain position even if one active component fails
Having multiple DPOs on the bridge at all times
The use of two different types of fuel in the generators
The presence of extra lifeboats on the vessel
items.explanation: Redundancy in DP (Equipment Class 2 and 3) ensures that no single failure in an active component will result in a loss of position.

items.situation: During cargo operations on a tankers, a shore-side loading arm begins to leak significantly onto the ship's deck near the manifold. The Watch Officer notices the spill spreading toward the scuppers. The cargo being loaded is high-volatility crude oil.
items.question: What do you do? Explain your actions in order.
key_steps: Activate the Emergency Stop (ESD) to cease all cargo transfer.
Raise the alarm and inform both the terminal and the Chief Officer.
Ensure all scuppers are effectively plugged and begin containing the spill with sawdust or oil spill kits.
Initiate the SOPEP/SMPEP procedures as required by the vessel's plan.
Ensure no hot work or potential ignition sources are near the spill area.
items.critical_step: Activate the Emergency Stop (ESD) to immediately stop the source of the leak.
items.regulation: MARPOL Annex I and ISGOTT (International Safety Guide for Oil Tankers and Terminals)

items.question: You are a 2nd Officer handover out to a 3rd Officer. You have a malfunctioning X-Band radar. How do you ensure an effective handover regarding this equipment?
key_steps: Physically demonstrate the specific fault or error code to the incoming officer
Clearly state what limitations this imposes on navigation and collision avoidance
Verify the incoming officer has noted the defect in the bridge log and understands the work-around
Confirm that the Master has been notified and a defect report is filed in the PMS
items.critical_step: Ensure the incoming officer acknowledges the specific operational limitations caused by the equipment failure.
items.regulation: STCW Section A-VIII/2, Part 4-1 (Principles to be observed in keeping a navigational watch)

items.question: While performing a cargo watch, you observe a rating performing a task in a manner that deviates from the approved SMS procedure but is 'faster'. How do you handle this?
key_steps: Intervene immediately to stop the unsafe act or deviation from procedure
Explain the specific risk and the requirement to follow the Safety Management System (SMS)
Direct the rating to restart the task using the approved method and equipment
Report the 'near-miss' or deviation to the Chief Officer to prevent recurrence
items.critical_step: Intervene immediately to stop the deviation from the approved SMS procedure.

items.question: The Master gives an order for a course change that you believe will bring the vessel dangerously close to a charted shoal. How do you communicate this concern?
key_steps: State the concern clearly and professionally using Closed-Loop Communication
Point out the specific hazard on the ECDIS or paper chart to the Master
Suggest an alternative course that maintains safety margins
If the risk is imminent and unaddressed, take emergency action to keep the ship in safe water
items.critical_step: Challenge the decision clearly and provide evidence of the hazard from navigational aids.
items.regulation: IMO Resolution A.893(21) (Guidelines for Voyage Planning)

items.question: You are leading a mooring station team. One member is not wearing their chin strap and is standing in a snap-back zone. How do you exercise leadership here?
key_steps: Use a 'Stop Work Authority' to halt the operation temporarily
Direct the crew member to adjust their PPE and move to a safe standing zone
Brief the entire team on the specific snap-back hazards of the current mooring configuration
Continue the operation only once all safety requirements are met
items.critical_step: Direct the crew member to move out of the snap-back zone before continuing operations.
items.regulation: COSWP (Code of Safe Working Practices) Chapter 26

items.situation: During cargo operations in port, you are the Duty Officer on deck. You notice a hydraulic hose on a deck crane has burst, spraying approximately 50 liters of hydraulic oil onto the deck, with some oil running toward the scuppers and potentially overboard.
items.question: What do you do? Explain your actions in order.
key_steps: Immediately press the emergency stop for the crane and notify the bunker/cargo team to stop operations.
Plug all scuppers and contain the spill on deck using sawdust, booms, or absorbent pads.
Inform the Master and the Chief Officer of the incident.
Initiate the SOPEP (Shipboard Oil Pollution Emergency Plan) reporting procedures.
Coordinate the cleanup and ensure no oil has reached the water.
items.critical_step: Contain the spill on deck to prevent oil from entering the water through scuppers or overboard discharges.

items.situation: You are conducting a routine safety inspection when you discover a seafarer entering a ballast tank without a permit-to-work or an attendant at the hatch. The seafarer appears dizzy and is leaning against the internal ladder.
items.question: What do you do? Explain your actions in order.
key_steps: Immediately shout to the seafarer to exit the space and prevent others from entering.
Raise the 'Enclosed Space Emergency' alarm on the PA system or radio.
Do not enter the space yourself to attempt a rescue without proper BA and equipment.
Prepare the rescue equipment (tripod, SCBA, stretcher) at the entrance.
Provide first aid and oxygen once the seafarer is safely extracted by the rescue team.
items.critical_step: Do not enter the enclosed space until the emergency rescue team with breathing apparatus arrives.
items.regulation: IMO Resolution A.1050(27) - Revised Recommendations for Entering Enclosed Spaces Aboard Ships

items.situation: While performing a routine inspection of the Lifeboat during your watch, you notice that the limit switch on the davit is corroded and fails to stop the winch when tested. The weekly safety inspection is due today. You are the designated Life-Saving Appliances (LSA) officer.
items.question: What do you do? Explain your actions in order.
key_steps: Isolate the power to the lifeboat winch to prevent accidental damage.
Label the equipment as 'Out of Service' or 'Defective'.
Report the defect immediately to the Chief Officer and the Master.
Raise a work order in the Planned Maintenance System (PMS).
Consult the manufacturer's manual for spare parts and repair procedures.
items.critical_step: Label the equipment as 'Out of Service' or 'Defective'.

items.situation: You are supervising an Ordinary Seaman (OS) painting the superstructure. You notice the OS has set up a ladder on a wet deck without a second person to steady it and is not wearing a safety harness despite working at a height of 3 meters.
items.question: What do you do? Explain your actions in order.
key_steps: Order the OS to stop work and descend the ladder immediately.
Conduct a 'Toolbox Talk' to explain the risks of falling and wet surfaces.
Ensure the OS puts on a safety harness and secures a fall arrestor.
Assign a second crew member to secure the base of the ladder.
Verify the Work at Height permit is correctly filled out and authorized.
items.critical_step: Order the OS to stop work and descend the ladder immediately.
items.regulation: Code of Safe Working Practices (COSWP) Chapter 17

items.question: While preparing for a bunker operation, you observe a senior officer bypassing the 'Bunker Checklist' to save time. How do you respond?
key_steps: Politely but firmly intervene and remind the officer of the mandatory nature of the checklist.
Refuse to sign the bunker safety check until all physical verifications are completed.
Escalate the matter to the Chief Officer or Master if the safety breach persists.
Document the non-conformity in accordance with the vessel's SMS.
items.critical_step: Politely but firmly intervene and remind the officer of the mandatory nature of the checklist.

items.question: A junior deck rating is performing a task incorrectly that could lead to a minor equipment failure. How do you exercise leadership in this situation?
key_steps: Stop the work immediately to prevent damage or injury.
Explain the correct procedure by referring to the relevant technical manual or SMS instruction.
Supervise the rating while they restart the task to ensure competency.
Provide constructive feedback later to encourage professional development.
items.critical_step: Explain the correct procedure by referring to the relevant technical manual or SMS instruction.
items.regulation: STCW Table A-II/1 - Leadership and Teamwork Skills

items.question: According to COLREG Rule 15, when two power-driven vessels are crossing so as to involve risk of collision, which vessel is required to keep out of the way?
options: The vessel which has the other on her own starboard side
The vessel which has the other on her own port side
The larger vessel with more limited maneuverability
The vessel that first detects the other on radar
items.explanation: Rule 15 states that the vessel which has the other on her own starboard side shall keep out of the way and shall, if the circumstances of the case admit, avoid crossing ahead of the other vessel.

items.question: When loading a bulk carrier, what is the 'Permissible Still Water Shear Force' (SWSF) limit intended to prevent?
options: Structural failure of the hull girder due to vertical load imbalances
Excessive rolling of the vessel in heavy seas
Localized denting of the tank top plating
Liquefaction of the cargo during the voyage
items.explanation: SWSF limits ensure that the vertical forces resulting from the distribution of weights and buoyancy do not exceed the design strength of the ship's longitudinal members.
items.regulation: SOLAS Chapter VI and IACS Unified Requirements

items.question: Which of the following operations must be recorded in the Oil Record Book Part I (Machinery Space Operations) for all ships above 400 GT?
options: Discharge of bilge water that has accumulated in machinery spaces
Loading of bulk grain cargo
Disposal of food waste at sea
Ballasting of dedicated clean ballast tanks
items.explanation: MARPOL Annex I requires that the discharge of machinery space bilge water be recorded in the Oil Record Book Part I.

items.question: In Dynamic Positioning (DP), what is the primary purpose of the 'Voting' logic in a triple redundant sensor system?
options: To identify and reject data from a single failed or drifting sensor
To allow the DPO to choose their favorite sensor manually
To average the errors of all sensors to create a new median position
To save power by turning off two of the three sensors
items.explanation: Voting logic compares inputs from three sensors; if one deviates significantly (fails), it is 'voted out' to prevent the system from following erroneous data.

items.question: While at anchor, the OOW notices the 'swing circle' on the GPS/ECDIS is consistently being breached and the COG/SOG indicate a steady 1.5 knots against the wind. What is the most likely immediate risk?
options: The vessel is dragging her anchor
The GPS signal is experiencing multi-path interference
The tide is changing direction
The anchor chain has become fouled around the bulbous bow
items.explanation: A steady speed over ground away from the anchor position while outside the swing circle is a primary indicator of a dragging anchor.

items.question: When securing a vessel with 'mixed mooring' (e.g., wire ropes and synthetic tails), why is it critical that all lines in the same service direction have similar elastic elongation properties?
options: To ensure that the load is distributed evenly across all lines
To prevent the wire ropes from rusting
To make it easier for the winches to heave in
To comply with the ship's aesthetic standards
items.explanation: Lines with different elasticity (e.g., a wire and a polypropylene rope) will not share the load; the stiffer line (wire) will take the entire load and potentially fail.

items.question: A cargo ship is navigating in a 'narrow channel'. According to COLREG Rule 9, a vessel of less than 20 meters in length shall not:
options: Impede the passage of a vessel which can safely navigate only within such channel
Enter the channel if a larger vessel is present
Cross the channel under any circumstances
Overtake any other vessel
items.explanation: Rule 9(b) specifically states that a vessel of less than 20 meters in length or a sailing vessel shall not impede the passage of a vessel which can safely navigate only within a narrow channel or fairway.

items.question: You are the OOW on a DP-2 vessel. A 'Red Alert' is triggered in the DP system. What is the required immediate action for the OOW/DPO?
options: Initiate emergency procedures and prepare to move the vessel clear of the installation/danger
Check the sensors to see if the alarm is a false positive
Wait for the Chief Engineer to come to the bridge
Acknowledge the alarm and continue current operations
items.explanation: A Red Alert indicates a loss of position or an imminent loss of position; safety of the personnel and the vessel is the priority, requiring immediate termination of operations.

items.question: During a passage, you need to execute a 'Wheel Over' point. If the vessel is heavily loaded, how will the 'Transfer' (the distance the ship moves perpendicular to the original course) compare to the light ballast condition?
options: The transfer will generally increase because of greater momentum and reduced rudder effectiveness
The transfer will decrease because the vessel is deeper in the water
The transfer will remain exactly the same regardless of draft
The transfer is only affected by the wind speed
items.explanation: A heavily loaded vessel has greater inertia and often a larger turning circle (advance and transfer) compared to the same vessel in a light ballast condition.
items.regulation: IMO Resolution A.751(18) / Bridge Procedures Guide
